job_location: 185 Fanshawe Street, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1010, New Zealand
responsibilities: Develop enduring, governed and trusted analytical foundations that make complex data accessible and business-readable.
Enable high-quality self-service and AI-assisted analytics, allowing teams to confidently discover, understand and use trusted data.
Design data with both people and AI in mind, ensuring analytical products are well structured, documented and ready for emerging AI use cases.
Partner with business and technical teams to turn complex, ambiguous problems into well-designed analytical solutions that deliver meaningful business outcomes.
Set and champion analytics engineering standards and patterns, improving the quality, consistency, reusability and maintainability of analytical products across the organisation.
Grow capability across the craft through technical leadership, coaching and knowledge sharing.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: bring robust, efficient, and trusted AI-ready data products and solutions to life
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Correctness vocabulary is the whole register - 'robust', 'trusted', 'governed', 'reliable, secure and scalable', 'quality, consistency, reusability and maintainability' - with no speed or shipping language at all.
evidence.domain_risk: including delivery of complex analytical solutions in an enterprise environment
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: An enterprise airline analytics function where governance is named as a design consideration, but with no financial-reporting, regulatory or audit framing, so errors affect business decisions rather than compliance.
evidence.collaboration_width: No distinctly named partner teams - only generic references to 'cross-functional squads', 'business and technical teams' and 'business leaders and SMEs'.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Set and champion analytics engineering standards and patterns, improving the quality, consistency, reusability and maintainability of analytical products across the organisation.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Organisation-wide analytics engineering standards, cross-functional squads and an explicit enterprise environment point to an established, specialised function operating at scale.
evidence.jd_authorship: Develop enduring, governed and trusted analytical foundations that make complex data accessible and business-readable.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Every bullet is an abstract capability statement with no named tool, scale figure or methodology anywhere in the posting - it could describe any senior analytics role.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Enable high-quality self-service and AI-assisted analytics, allowing teams to confidently discover, understand and use trusted data.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The primary audience is the data function's own consumers - self-service analytics users, semantic layers and downstream AI - rather than a specific commercial or finance partner.
evidence.autonomy_level: Set and champion analytics engineering standards and patterns
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role sets organisation-wide standards, shapes roadmaps and prioritises opportunities, and grows craft capability through technical leadership.
evidence.ai_role: Design data with both people and AI in mind, ensuring analytical products are well structured, documented and ready for emerging AI use cases.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate must build AI-ready data foundations that support machine consumption for AI, ML and generative AI use cases - the AI sits downstream of their output.
evidence.testing_framing: Set and champion analytics engineering standards and patterns, improving the quality, consistency, reusability and maintainability of analytical products across the organisation.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Quality is framed as something the candidate sets and champions organisation-wide rather than a tool in a skills list, though no specific testing tool is named.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: translating business questions into trusted analytical models while building the reliable, secure and scalable foundations those models depend on
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Trust is the dominant framing from the role summary onward - 'trusted' appears five times - and the fear is unreliable data products reaching the organisation's decision-makers and AI systems.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: We need Senior Analytics Engineers to work in cross-functional squads and bring robust, efficient, and trusted AI-ready data products and solutions to life.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The dominant verbs are develop, enable, design, set and champion - creating new foundations, standards and AI-ready products rather than repairing existing ones.

evidence.loss_aversion: Develop enduring, governed and trusted analytical foundations that make complex data accessible and business-readable - the repeated trust and governance framing signals that the fear is untrusted analytical products spreading across the organisation.
